clinician.trajectory_summary: A 58-year-old patient presented with a three-month history of the classic triad of pneumaturia, fecaluria, and dysuria/burning micturition with recurrent cystitis episodes, unresponsive to antibiotics. On admission, the patient was vitally stable. Ultrasound imaging demonstrated a 1.5 cm defect between the sigmoid colon and urinary bladder with passage of echogenic material into the bladder, distinguishable from ureteric jets. Exploratory laparotomy revealed significant adhesions between the sigmoid colon and urinary bladder with necrotic tissue and multiple diverticula along the connection. Histopathological examination of the resected specimen confirmed non-specific chronic inflammatory process consistent with diverticulitis and excluded malignancy. Definitive treatment consisted of recto-sigmoidectomy (approximately 15 cm) with proximal segment colostomy.
